Ketamine Water Vapor
I was doing Ketamine with a friend (SeriusB). We both agreed that snorting it was painful, damaging the sinuses and causing a lot of rejection as the nose rejected and sneezed and dripped it back out before much is absorbed, smoking it allowed greater consumption but again we hit a wall as we're fighting to keep the smoke inside our lungs, the gag reflex reacts and we expel much of we inhale, so it is very inefficient.
SeriusB found a solution, he put a few water droplets on the ketamine powder, gave it a few seconds to let it absorb the water, so it was damp but not not slurry or liquid more like wet cement and used a lighter to heat it. It melts releasing the water vapor allowing us to inhale much greater quantities
That water vapor mixed with ketamine was much smoother coming in, it allowed for deep hits and there was no gag reflex
That water vapor mixed with ketamine was much smoother coming in, it allowed for deep hits and there was no gag reflex
, and we can take it all in, we can consume much more ketamine that way, and it lasted much longer by about 3 times, i.e. 10-15 minutes usual ketamine at its peak, and with this method the peak lasted for approximate an hour.
Personally for me, it lasted an hour with the expected ketamine effects, loss of body image, couldn't tell where my limbs were or where my head connected, loss of depth perception, sound hallucinations (TV static and waves) and also a bit of visual effects as if I saw the electromagnetic spectrum emanating from the electrical objects. The increased consumption produced much stronger and more vivid hallucinations and lasted longer, as well as the dissociative effects, and allowed for much greater consumption as my body wasn't rejecting it.
SeriusB, who is experienced with different substances, and ketamine included, passed out from it for the first time due to much larger intake, he consumed a much greater quantity than he could ever before. Describing what he felt, he says that he first went into a deep dream state, BEFORE actually going to sleep.
